descriptionChirho: Unrestrained, shameless immorality — licentiousness, sensuality, debauchery. All three clusters represent the same abstract noun denoting excessive sexual indulgence or moral abandon, differing only in case and number. Spanish uses 'lascivia', 'libertinaje', 'licencias', and 'desenfrenos' — all in the same semantic field of moral excess; Arabic 'دَعارَةٍ' (da'āra = prostitution/debauchery) and 'فجور' (fujūr = immorality) throughout; Korean '음란' (ŭmnan = lewdness/obscenity) consistently; Hindi 'लम्पटता' (lampaṭatā = lechery) and 'लुच्चपन' (luccapan = wantonness); Swahili uses 'ufisadi' (corruption/immorality) uniformly across all three clusters, confirming a single sense.
